name: checkout
title: The Till
description: Checkout form as a shop till: the order summary is the till tape — every line item, shipping, and tax with the total computed from the visible lines, never changed at the last step — and the payment form is one page in three numbered steps with guest checkout by default, no pre-ticked extras, and a PAID stamp on submit.

import * as React from "react"; import { cn } from "../lib/utils"; /** * The Till — a checkout form staged as a shop till. * The order summary is the till tape on the left: every line item, the * shipping, and the tax, with the total computed from the visible lines — * never typed in, and never changed at the last step. The payment form is * the till itself on the right: one page, three numbered steps (Contact, * Shipping, Payment), seven fields and nothing more. Guest checkout is the * default — no account is created, and the small print says an account can * be made after the order, when all it takes is a password. Gift wrap is * an unchecked box, never a pre-ticked extra, and ticking it recomputes * the total in front of you. Billing defaults to the shipping address * because that is what most people want, and the box says so plainly. * Submitting prints a PAID stamp and the order number in place — wiring * the charge to a real payment processor is the integrator's job, and the * optional `onPay` prop is where that hook lives. This is a demo till: * no card is charged and no number leaves the page. Flat paper, ink, * till red, static except for the form itself. The till stays paper in * both modes — a receipt is printed. */ export interface TillItem { name: string; detail: string; qty: number; /** unit price in dollars */ unitPrice: number; } export interface TillProps { kicker?: string; heading?: string; standfirst?: string; /** the shop's name, printed at the head of the tape */ shopName?: string; /** the order number printed on the tape; a demo starting point */ orderNumber?: string; items?: TillItem[]; shippingLabel?: string; shippingCost?: number; taxLabel?: string; /** tax rate as a decimal, e.g. 0.0825 for 8.25% */ taxRate?: number; /** when the order arrives, printed on the tape */ deliveryDate?: string; /** gift-wrap price; the box is unchecked by default */ giftWrapPrice?: number; /** called with the order total on submit, when the integrator wires up a real processor */ onPay?: (details: { email: string; total: number }) => void; footnote?: string; className?: string; } function money(n: number): string { return `$${n.toFixed(2)}`; } export function Till({ kicker = "The till · one page, no surprises", heading = "Pay for what's on the tape.", standfirst = "The total above is the total you pay. No fee appears at the last step, no account is required, and the form asks for seven fields — everything it needs to send the order, nothing it doesn't.", shopName = "The Unslop General Store", orderNumber = "1042", items = [ { name: "Field notebook, dot grid", detail: "A6 · 96 pages · paper that takes ink", qty: 1, unitPrice: 24.0 }, { name: "Brass paper clips", detail: "Box of 100 · they do not rust", qty: 2, unitPrice: 9.5 }, ], shippingLabel = "Shipping · Standard, tracked", shippingCost = 6.95, taxLabel = "Sales tax", taxRate = 0.0825, deliveryDate = "Thursday, November 26", giftWrapPrice = 4.0, onPay, footnote, className, }: TillProps) { const [email, setEmail] = React.useState(""); const [name, setName] = React.useState(""); const [street, setStreet] = React.useState(""); const [city, setCity] = React.useState(""); const [zip, setZip] = React.useState(""); const [cardName, setCardName] = React.useState(""); const [cardNumber, setCardNumber] = React.useState(""); const [expiry, setExpiry] = React.useState(""); const [cvc, setCvc] = React.useState(""); const [giftWrap, setGiftWrap] = React.useState(false); const [billingSame, setBillingSame] = React.useState(true); const [paid, setPaid] = React.useState(false); const subtotal = items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.qty * item.unitPrice, 0); const wrap = giftWrap ? giftWrapPrice : 0; const tax = Math.round((subtotal + wrap) * taxRate * 100) / 100; const total = subtotal + shippingCost + wrap + tax; const formatCardNumber = (value: string) => value.replace(/\D/g, "").slice(0, 16).replace(/(\d{4})(?=\d)/g, "$1 "); const formatExpiry = (value: string) => { const digits = value.replace(/\D/g, "").slice(0, 4); return digits.length > 2 ? `${digits.slice(0, 2)}/${digits.slice(2)}` : digits; }; const submit = (e: React.FormEvent) => { e.preventDefault(); if (!email.trim() || !name.trim() || !cardNumber.replace(/\D/g, "")) return; onPay?.({ email: email.trim(), total }); setPaid(true); }; return (

    {[ ["01", "Contact", "Where the receipt goes"], ["02", "Shipping", "Where the parcel goes"], ["03", "Payment", "The card, and nothing else"], ].map(([num, step, what]) => (

    2. ))}

One page, start to finish. The steps are labels, not a maze — nothing hides behind a “next” button.

Order Nº {orderNumber} · arrives {deliveryDate}

    {items.map((item) => (
  • {item.name} {item.qty > 1 ? ` × ${item.qty}` : ""} {item.detail} {money(item.qty * item.unitPrice)}
    • ))}
  • {shippingLabel} {money(shippingCost)}
    • {giftWrap && (
  • Gift wrap {money(giftWrapPrice)}
    • )}
  • {taxLabel} ({(taxRate * 100).toFixed(2)}%) {money(tax)}

Total due {money(total)}

This total is the sum of the lines above it. Nothing is added after you press pay.

setExpiry(formatExpiry(e.target.value))} placeholder="MM/YY" className="mt-2 w-full min-w-0 border-2 border-stone-900 bg-[#f6f1e7] px-4 py-3 font-serif text-lg text-stone-900 placeholder:text-stone-400 focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-red-800" />
setCvc(e.target.value.replace(/\D/g, "").slice(0, 4))} placeholder="123" className="mt-2 w-full min-w-0 border-2 border-stone-900 bg-[#f6f1e7] px-4 py-3 font-serif text-lg text-stone-900 placeholder:text-stone-400 focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-red-800" />
)}

No account, no pre-ticked extras, no fee at the last step. This till is a demo — wire onPay to your real payment processor. No card is charged here, and no number leaves this page.

A checkout that shows its working, then asks for the card.
